laws.title: 0.03% BAC Driving Limit
laws.subtitle: Japan's road traffic law applies equally in Osaka
laws.fullDescription: Osaka's drivers are subject to the same Road Traffic Act (道路交通法) BAC limit of 0.03% as the rest of Japan. The Osaka Prefectural Police (大阪府警察) actively enforces this on the Hanshin Expressway network, surface roads, and near the entertainment district of Dotonbori, where drink-driving accidents involving tourists are monitored. The Keiji region (Osaka, Kyoto, Kobe) has historically higher enforcement rates.
laws.penalty: Up to 3 years imprisonment or ¥500,000 fine; licence suspension for BAC 0.03–0.08%; revocation above 0.08%
exceptions: Zero tolerance effectively applies to commercial/professional drivers

quiz.q: Japan's BAC driving limit of 0.03% — how does it compare to the UK's 0.08% limit?
quiz.explanation: Japan's 0.03% limit is more than 2.5× stricter than the UK's 0.08% — nearly the lowest in the world.

laws.title: Dotonbori Public Conduct Ordinance
laws.subtitle: Osaka's entertainment district has special crowd rules
laws.fullDescription: Osaka's Minami district, centred on Dotonbori, is famous for rowdy New Year celebrations where crowds historically jumped from the Ebisubashi bridge into the Dotonbori Canal. Osaka Prefectural Police and the city's special ordinances prohibit diving from the bridge, regulate street drinking hours in Namba, and restrict busking without permits. The Glico Running Man and other Dotonbori icons are municipal property subject to damage penalties.
laws.penalty: Bridge-jumping: fine ¥50,000 under public nuisance ordinance; busking without permit: ¥30,000 fine
exceptions: Permitted festival events with city approval

quiz.q: What famous Osaka tradition does the city's ordinance now prohibit?
options: Jumping from Ebisubashi bridge into the Dotonbori Canal
quiz.explanation: Jumping from Ebisubashi into the Dotonbori Canal — once a popular celebration — is now prohibited under Osaka's public conduct ordinances.

laws.title: Osaka IR Casino Development Zone
laws.subtitle: Japan's first legal casino resort approved for Osaka
laws.fullDescription: Osaka's Integrated Resort (IR) development plan — approved by the national government in 2023 — will establish Japan's first legal casino resort on Yumeshima (夢洲) artificial island, targeting a 2030 opening coinciding with Expo 2025. The IR Promotion Act (IR整備法) permits gambling within the complex, surrounded by casino entry taxes of ¥6,000 per entry for Japanese nationals (free for foreigners). Osaka's special economic zone designation governs construction and operations.
laws.penalty: Illegal casino operation outside IR zone: up to 3 years imprisonment; entry tax evasion by Japanese nationals: fines
exceptions: Foreign passport holders exempt from the ¥6,000 entry fee

quiz.q: Where in Osaka is Japan's first legal casino resort being developed?
quiz.explanation: Japan's first IR casino resort is being built on Yumeshima (夢洲) artificial island in Osaka Bay, targeting a 2030 opening.

laws.title: Takoyaki and Street Food Hygiene Standards
laws.subtitle: Street vendors require food hygiene certification
laws.fullDescription: Osaka is the birthplace of takoyaki (たこ焼き) and a global street food culture icon. All food vendors — including festival stall operators at Osaka's numerous matsuri — must comply with the Food Sanitation Act (食品衛生法) and hold a Osaka Prefecture food hygiene certification. Temporary stalls at major events (Tenjin Matsuri, etc.) require additional temporary establishment permits from the Namba Health Centre. Mobile food trucks have separate licencing since 2021 reform.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed food vending: fines up to ¥500,000; hygiene violations: closure orders and up to 2 years imprisonment
exceptions: Truly temporary charitable/school events with pre-approval
laws.sourceLabel: Osaka Prefecture Health Department — Food Sanitation

quiz.q: What famous ball-shaped street food originated in Osaka?
quiz.explanation: Takoyaki (たこ焼き) — octopus balls — was invented in Osaka's Naniwa ward and remains the city's most iconic street food.

laws.title: Osaka Bay Coastal Management Act
laws.subtitle: Land reclamation and industrial discharge regulated
laws.fullDescription: Osaka Bay, site of major industrial reclamation since the postwar period, is regulated under the Coast Act (海岸法) and Osaka's own Bay Area Environmental Plan. The Yodo River feeding into the bay is Japan's most heavily used river per capita; its water quality is monitored under the Water Pollution Prevention Act (水質汚濁防止法). Industrial dischargers must report and meet effluent standards. Osaka has improved bay water quality significantly since the 1960s high-pollution era.
laws.penalty: Industrial discharge exceeding limits: up to 6 months imprisonment or ¥1,000,000 fine
exceptions: Emergency overflow events with immediate reporting

quiz.q: Which river, flowing through Osaka into Osaka Bay, is Japan's most heavily used per capita?
quiz.explanation: The Yodo River (淀川) supplies water to Osaka and the greater Kansai region — Japan's most heavily utilised river per person.

laws.title: Osaka Regional Minimum Wage
laws.subtitle: Second-highest minimum wage in Japan after Tokyo
laws.fullDescription: Osaka's regional minimum wage, set by the Osaka Labour Bureau annually, is consistently one of Japan's highest. As of October 2024, it stands at ¥1,114 per hour — second only to Tokyo's ¥1,163. Osaka's large service sector, including restaurants, retail, and hospitality focused on domestic and inbound tourism, is the primary setting for minimum wage compliance enforcement.
laws.penalty: Employers paying below minimum: fines up to ¥500,000
exceptions: Apprenticeship exceptions require application to Labour Bureau

quiz.q: How does Osaka's minimum wage rank nationally in Japan?
quiz.explanation: Osaka's minimum wage is second-highest in Japan after Tokyo — reflecting its status as the country's second major economic centre.

laws.title: Knife Carry Law — Same as National Standard
laws.subtitle: Blades over 6cm prohibited in public
laws.fullDescription: Osaka's enforcement of the Firearms and Swords Control Law is particularly active given the city's historically higher violent crime rate compared to Tokyo. The Namba and Shinsaibashi entertainment districts see regular police stop-and-search operations targeting knife carrying. Osaka has also seen yakuza-related knife crimes — the prefecture operates a dedicated organised crime suppression division.
laws.penalty: Up to 2 years imprisonment or ¥300,000 fine for carrying blades over 6cm in public
exceptions: Professional use (chefs, tradespeople) with demonstrable need

quiz.q: Compared to Tokyo, Osaka historically has:
quiz.explanation: Osaka has historically recorded higher violent crime rates than Tokyo, partly related to yakuza activity in the Kansai region.

laws.title: Pachinko Density — Osaka Concentration
laws.subtitle: Osaka has Japan's highest pachinko parlour density
laws.fullDescription: Osaka Prefecture has the highest concentration of pachinko parlours per capita in Japan. Under the Act on Control and Improvement of Amusement Business (風営法), parlours must be licenced by the prefectural public safety commission (公安委員会). Machines are capped at payout rates to prevent excessive gambling behaviour. Osaka's 2023 IR discussions highlighted tension between the existing pachinko industry and incoming casino competition.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed operation: up to 3 years imprisonment; machine manipulation: up to 5 years
exceptions: Out-of-scope: legal horse/boat racing
laws.sourceLabel: Osaka Prefectural Police — Amusement Business Licensing

quiz.q: Which body issues pachinko parlour licences in Osaka?
options: Prefectural Public Safety Commission (公安委員会)
quiz.explanation: Pachinko parlours are licenced by the Prefectural Public Safety Commission (公安委員会) under the Amusement Business Control Act.

laws.title: Osaka Indoor Smoking Regulations
laws.subtitle: Aligned with national 2020 health promotion changes
laws.fullDescription: Osaka implemented the national Health Promotion Act indoor smoking ban in line with Tokyo for the 2020 Olympics period. However, enforcement in Osaka's dense restaurant and izakaya (居酒屋) districts has been noted by health inspectors as less rigorous than in Tokyo, given the local hospitality culture ('kuidaore' — eat yourself bankrupt). Osaka City operates its own inspection programme separate from prefecture.
laws.penalty: Businesses: up to ¥500,000 fine; individuals violating in prohibited areas: ¥30,000 fine
exceptions: Outdoor designated smoking areas
Hotels with designated smoking floors
laws.sourceLabel: Osaka City Health Department — Smoking Regulations

quiz.q: What is the Osaka cultural phrase for eating extravagantly until you go broke?
quiz.explanation: Kuidaore (食い倒れ) — 'eat yourself bankrupt' — reflects Osaka's identity as Japan's food capital and explains the city's vibrant restaurant culture.

laws.title: Osaka Waste Separation System
laws.subtitle: Four-category waste separation required
laws.fullDescription: Osaka City requires residents to separate waste into four main categories: burnable (可燃ごみ), non-burnable (不燃ごみ), resource recyclables (資源ごみ), and large items (粗大ごみ). Collection schedules vary by ward. Osaka's Rinkai Kousoku Tetsudo (Osaka Metro) system stations display waste sorting instructions. Osaka Prefecture operates the Maishima Incineration Plant (designed by Friedensreich Hundertwasser) which handles a significant portion of burnable waste.
laws.penalty: Improper disposal: ¥2,000–¥30,000 fines; bulk illegal dumping: up to ¥1,000,000
exceptions: Industrial waste handled under separate Industrial Waste Management Act

quiz.q: Who designed Osaka's visually distinctive Maishima Incineration Plant?
quiz.explanation: Osaka's Maishima Incineration Plant was co-designed by Austrian artist Friedensreich Hundertwasser, giving it a colourful, organic appearance.

laws.title: Osaka City LGBT Partnership Scheme
laws.subtitle: Partnership certificates since 2020
laws.fullDescription: Osaka City introduced its partnership certificate system (パートナーシップ宣誓制度) in January 2020, ahead of Tokyo's 2022 scheme, making it one of Japan's earliest major city adopters. Osaka Prefecture followed with its own scheme. Certificates provide practical recognition for hospital visiting rights, public housing applications, and some employer benefits. As of 2024, all of Osaka Prefecture's municipalities offer some form of recognition.
laws.penalty: N/A — rights-granting provision
exceptions: National marriage law remains between opposite-sex couples

quiz.q: Which major Japanese city introduced its LGBT partnership certificate scheme first — Osaka or Tokyo?
quiz.explanation: Osaka City introduced its partnership certificate scheme in January 2020 — Tokyo followed in November 2022.

laws.title: Osaka Metro IC Card System
laws.subtitle: Osaka Pitapa vs national Suica/Pasmo
laws.fullDescription: Osaka's public transport uses the Pitapa (ピタパ) post-payment IC card system for Osaka Metro, as well as accepting Suica and Pasmo. Unlike Suica/Pasmo (prepaid top-up), Pitapa is a credit-linked system. Since 2023, Osaka Metro also accepts QR code tickets — a first among major Japanese metro systems. Fare evasion on Osaka Metro is prosecuted under the same theft/fraud provisions as Tokyo.
laws.penalty: Fare evasion: back-fare + surcharge; criminal: up to 10 years (theft/fraud provisions)

quiz.q: What distinguishes Osaka's Pitapa IC card from Tokyo's Suica?
options: Pitapa is prepaid, Suica is post-payment
Pitapa is post-payment/credit-linked; Suica is prepaid top-up
They are identical systems with different branding
quiz.explanation: Pitapa is a credit-linked post-payment system unique to Kansai, while Suica and Pasmo are prepaid top-up cards.

laws.title: Minpaku (Airbnb) Local Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Osaka City has stricter rules than national minimum
laws.fullDescription: Under Japan's Minpaku Law (2018), Osaka City additionally restricts short-term rentals in residential zones to weekends only (Friday–Sunday) in certain wards. Dotonbori and Namba-area rentals in tourist zones have fewer restrictions. Osaka was an early adopter of registration requirements and operates one of Japan's largest minpaku databases. The city saw a 70% cancellation rate from hosts when the law took effect in June 2018 — a significant market disruption.
laws.penalty: Unregistered operation: up to ¥1,000,000 fine; operating in restricted zone: rental suspension orders
exceptions: Ryokan and hotel licences under Hotel Business Act operate normally

quiz.q: What happened to Osaka's Airbnb market when Japan's Minpaku Law took effect in June 2018?
quiz.explanation: Approximately 70% of Osaka's Airbnb listings were cancelled when the Minpaku Law took effect — hosts couldn't meet registration requirements.

laws.title: Osaka Financial Exchange (OFX) Regulation
laws.subtitle: Derivatives and FX trading regulated by FSA
laws.fullDescription: The Osaka Exchange (大阪取引所), part of Japan Exchange Group (JPX) after a 2013 merger with Tokyo Stock Exchange, hosts all Japanese equity derivatives trading. Nikkei 225 futures are the world's most actively traded stock index futures contracts. The Financial Services Agency regulates all trading under the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act. Osaka historically hosted Japan's rice commodity exchange — the world's first futures market (established 1697).
laws.penalty: Market manipulation: up to 10 years imprisonment; fraud: up to ¥10,000,000 fine

quiz.q: Osaka hosted the world's first futures market in 1697 — what commodity was traded?
quiz.explanation: Osaka's Dōjima Rice Exchange (堂島米会所), established in 1697, is widely recognised as the world's first organised futures market.

laws.title: Yakuza Exclusion — Kansai Focus
laws.subtitle: Yamaguchi-gumi headquartered in Kobe, active in Osaka
laws.fullDescription: The Osaka Prefectural Organised Crime Group Exclusion Ordinance (暴力団排除条例, 2011) mirrors Tokyo's version but targets Kansai-based groups. The Yamaguchi-gumi (headquartered in Kobe) and its Osaka-active subsidiary groups are designated. Osaka's entertainment and real estate industries face specific anti-yakuza clauses. The city maintains a yakuza exclusion database for public housing applicants.
laws.penalty: Businesses providing benefits to yakuza: fines up to ¥5,000,000 and public naming

quiz.q: Where is Japan's largest yakuza organisation, the Yamaguchi-gumi, headquartered?
quiz.explanation: The Yamaguchi-gumi is headquartered in Kobe — but its activities extend throughout Kansai, including Osaka's entertainment districts.

laws.title: Nankai Trough Tsunami Preparedness
laws.subtitle: Osaka faces 30m tsunami risk from megaquake scenario
laws.fullDescription: Government assessments estimate a magnitude 9 Nankai Trough earthquake (南海トラフ地震) — with 70–80% probability within 30 years — could send a 3–5m tsunami into Osaka Bay within 90 minutes. In worst-case modelling, central Osaka could see flooding up to 3m deep. Osaka has invested ¥400 billion in seawall upgrades and evacuation tower infrastructure. Residents in designated tsunami hazard zones are registered in evacuation protocols.
laws.penalty: Failure to comply with official evacuation orders during declared emergencies: fines under Disaster Countermeasures Basic Act
laws.sourceLabel: Osaka Prefecture — Nankai Trough Disaster Plan

quiz.q: How much time would Osaka have before tsunami waves arrived after a Nankai Trough megaquake?
quiz.explanation: Government modelling estimates Osaka Bay would receive tsunami waves approximately 90 minutes after a Nankai Trough megaquake.

laws.title: Osaka府立 School Governance Reform
laws.subtitle: Osaka Ishin no Kai education reforms — school choice expanded
laws.fullDescription: Under Osaka Ishin no Kai (Osaka Restoration Association) governance since 2008, Osaka Prefecture implemented major education reforms including school choice policies, external evaluation of teachers, and integration of prefectural and Osaka City school administration. The Osaka Municipal University and Osaka Prefecture University were merged into Osaka Metropolitan University (大阪公立大学) in 2022 — Japan's largest public university by student numbers.
laws.penalty: N/A — administrative reform law; compulsory education failure to enrol: fines as per national standard

quiz.q: What new institution was created in 2022 by merging Osaka's two major public universities?
options: Osaka Metropolitan University (大阪公立大学)
quiz.explanation: Osaka Metropolitan University (大阪公立大学) formed in 2022 through the merger of Osaka Municipal and Osaka Prefecture Universities — Japan's largest public university.

laws.title: Tenjin Matsuri Public Safety Rules
laws.subtitle: Japan's top festival regulated for crowd safety
laws.fullDescription: The Tenjin Matsuri (天神祭), held on July 24–25 and considered one of Japan's top three festivals, draws over 1.3 million visitors to Osaka. The city enacts temporary public safety zones along the Okawa River route, restricts alcohol consumption in certain areas, and requires fire/fireworks display operators to hold pyrotechnics licences under the Fire Service Act (消防法). The river parade (船渡御) involves over 100 vessels subject to maritime safety rules.
laws.penalty: Illegal fireworks: up to 3 years imprisonment; crowd violation zones: fines per ordinance; unlicensed riverside stalls: closure
exceptions: Shrine and traditional participants exempt from some pedestrian traffic rules

quiz.q: Approximately how many people attend the Tenjin Matsuri festival in Osaka?
quiz.explanation: The Tenjin Matsuri attracts over 1.3 million visitors over two days — making it one of Japan's largest and most logistically complex festivals.

laws.title: Expo 2025 Data Collection Rules
laws.subtitle: Osaka Expo piloting facial recognition with consent framework
laws.fullDescription: Osaka's Expo 2025 (April–October 2025, Yumeshima) is piloting data collection systems including facial recognition for entry management, using consent-based frameworks under the Personal Information Protection Act (APPI). Expo operators, under guidance from Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission, must obtain explicit consent, store data for no longer than necessary, and provide access and deletion rights. This is Japan's largest single-event data protection compliance exercise.
laws.penalty: APPI violations at Expo: up to ¥100,000,000 corporate fines; individual: up to ¥1,000,000 fine
exceptions: Security emergency imaging with post-event notification
laws.sourceLabel: Japan Association for the 2025 World Exposition

quiz.q: Where in Osaka is Expo 2025 being held?
quiz.explanation: Expo 2025 is held on Yumeshima (夢洲) — the same artificial island that will later host Osaka's IR casino resort.

laws.title: Stimulant Drug Enforcement — Osaka
laws.subtitle: Osaka historically a major drug trafficking hub
laws.fullDescription: Osaka's port and proximity to Korea and China historically made it a major entry point for methamphetamine. The Osaka Prefectural Police narcotics division operates one of Japan's largest anti-stimulant drug enforcement units. The Stimulants Control Act (覚醒剤取締法) applies nationally; Osaka cases represent approximately 20% of all Japan stimulant arrests despite being ~8% of population — indicating elevated enforcement and trafficking levels.
laws.penalty: Possession: up to 10 years; trafficking: up to life imprisonment

quiz.q: Why has Osaka historically been a major drug trafficking entry point?
options: Osaka's port location and proximity to Korea and China
Its status as Japan's pharmaceutical manufacturing hub
quiz.explanation: Osaka's port and geographic proximity to Korea and China historically made it a primary entry point for methamphetamine into Japan.

laws.title: Tattoo Practice Licensing — Osaka Ruling
laws.subtitle: Supreme Court ruling: tattooing is not medical practice
laws.fullDescription: In 2020, Japan's Supreme Court overturned an Osaka lower court ruling that had convicted a tattoo artist for practising medicine without a licence. The Supreme Court held that tattooing is a traditional art form, not medical practice, and thus does not require a medical licence. This ruling reversed years of legal uncertainty for Japan's tattoo industry and set a national precedent. Osaka has the highest concentration of professional tattoo studios in Japan.
laws.penalty: Pre-2020: medical licence violations (up to 3 years); post-ruling: tattooing itself is no longer a criminal act for non-medical practitioners
exceptions: Permanent makeup for medical purposes requires medical licence
laws.sourceLabel: Supreme Court of Japan — 2020 Tattoo Ruling

quiz.q: What did Japan's 2020 Supreme Court rule about tattooing?
options: It is illegal for non-Japanese practitioners
It is a traditional art, not medical practice — no medical licence required
It must be performed in registered studios only
quiz.explanation: Japan's Supreme Court ruled in 2020 that tattooing is a traditional art form, overturning convictions of Osaka tattoo artists.

laws.title: Osaka 36 Agreement Compliance
laws.subtitle: Overtime tracking required with Tokyo-equivalent standards
laws.fullDescription: Osaka's Labour Standards Inspection Offices (労働基準監督署) enforce the same 36 Agreement overtime caps as national law (45 hours/month, 360 hours/year). Osaka's manufacturing sector (chemicals, precision equipment, food processing) and retail sector are priority enforcement targets. The Osaka Labour Bureau's 2023 enforcement data showed Osaka companies had the third-highest rate of overtime violations nationally.
laws.penalty: Employers: up to 6 months imprisonment or ¥300,000 fine for violation of agreed overtime caps
exceptions: Construction and transport industries had phase-in until April 2024

quiz.q: What is the standard monthly overtime cap under Japan's 36 Agreement framework?
quiz.explanation: Japan's Work Style Reform Act caps general overtime at 45 hours per month and 360 hours per year under 36 Agreements.

laws.title: Nikkei 225 Derivatives Trading Rules
laws.subtitle: World's most traded stock index futures — Osaka regulated
laws.fullDescription: The Osaka Exchange hosts Nikkei 225 futures and options — Japan's benchmark stock index derivatives. Under the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act, position limits, reporting thresholds, and margin requirements are set by the Japan Exchange Group (JPX). High-frequency trading (HFT) firms operating on Osaka Exchange must register as electronic trading system users. The 2013 Tokyo-Osaka exchange merger concentrated all equity derivatives in Osaka.
laws.penalty: Position limit violations: cease-and-desist; market manipulation: up to 10 years imprisonment
exceptions: Delta-neutral hedging positions exempt from some limits

quiz.q: What happened to Japan's equity derivatives market after the 2013 Tokyo-Osaka exchange merger?
options: Moved to a neutral digital platform
quiz.explanation: The 2013 merger of Tokyo and Osaka exchanges (creating JPX) concentrated all equity derivatives trading in Osaka's exchange.

laws.title: Osaka's Retail Discount Culture — Legal Limits
laws.subtitle: Discount vouchers and price reductions regulated
laws.fullDescription: Osaka's commercial culture of aggressive discounting ('makeppuri,' 'ne-giri' bargaining in markets like Kuromon Ichiba) intersects with the Act against Unjustifiable Premiums and Misleading Representations. Retailers cannot display a 'regular price' that was never actually charged. The Consumer Affairs Agency has investigated Osaka retailers — particularly in electronics (Den-Den Town) and food markets — for fake reference pricing.
laws.penalty: Fake reference pricing: cease-and-desist orders; fines up to 3% of related sales
exceptions: Genuine clearance sales of stock at original purchase price
laws.sourceLabel: Consumer Affairs Agency — Price Display Rules

quiz.q: Osaka's Den-Den Town is Japan's equivalent of which Tokyo electronics district?
quiz.explanation: Den-Den Town (でんでんタウン) in Nipponbashi, Osaka is the Kansai equivalent of Tokyo's Akihabara — electronics, gaming, and anime retail.

laws.title: Osaka Ferry and Water Taxi Rules
laws.subtitle: Osaka's canal network subject to maritime safety rules
laws.fullDescription: Osaka's historic network of canals (once called the 'Venice of the East') supports a growing tourism water transport sector. Water taxis and aqua buses operating on the Okawa, Dotonbori, and Namba canals require licences from the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism under the Maritime Safety Act. Life jackets are compulsory. The revived water transport network targets 1 million annual riders by 2030.
laws.penalty: Operating without maritime licence: up to 1 year imprisonment; life jacket non-provision: administrative fines
exceptions: Unpowered traditional boats at permitted festivals

quiz.q: What historical nickname was once given to Osaka because of its extensive canal network?
quiz.explanation: Osaka was known as 'the Venice of the East' (水都大阪) for its extensive historical canal network — much of which has been restored for tourism.

laws.title: Osaka Castle Park Conservation Zone
laws.subtitle: Development around historic park tightly restricted
laws.fullDescription: Osaka Castle Park (大阪城公園) and its surrounding Special Historical Zone are designated under both Japan's Cultural Properties Protection Law and Osaka City's Urban Park Act implementation. Development, advertising signage heights, and tree removal within the zone require city approval. The 2017 public-private partnership (Park Management Team) revitalized the park's facilities while maintaining conservation rules. The castle's inner compound is a National Special Historic Site.
laws.penalty: Unapproved development in historic zone: demolition orders + fines up to ¥1,000,000
exceptions: Emergency public works with notification

quiz.q: What type of landmark designation protects Osaka Castle's inner compound?
quiz.explanation: Osaka Castle's inner compound is designated a National Special Historic Site (国の特別史跡) — Japan's highest category of historic site protection.

laws.title: Zainichi Korean Community Legal Status
laws.subtitle: Special Permanent Resident status for long-term Korean residents
laws.fullDescription: Osaka has the largest Zainichi Korean (在日コリアン) community in Japan — approximately 120,000 people, concentrated in the Tsuruhashi and Ikuno districts. Special Permanent Resident (特別永住者) status, established under the 1991 Japan-Korea Memorandum, grants residence rights to Koreans and their descendants who came to Japan before WWII. Holders are exempt from regular residency card renewal cycles but are still foreign nationals without automatic citizenship.
laws.penalty: N/A — status grant, not penalty; violations of residence conditions: deportation proceedings
exceptions: Naturalisation is possible under standard procedures — approximately 10,000 Zainichi naturalise per year nationwide
laws.sourceLabel: Ministry of Justice — Special Permanent Residents

quiz.q: Which area of Osaka has Japan's largest Zainichi Korean community?
quiz.explanation: Osaka's Tsuruhashi and Ikuno districts host Japan's largest Zainichi Korean community — home to vibrant Korean commercial and cultural life.

laws.title: Osaka District Court — Major Trial Jurisdiction
laws.subtitle: Handles serious Kansai criminal and civil cases
laws.fullDescription: Osaka District Court (大阪地方裁判所) is Japan's second-largest district court by caseload. It has jurisdiction over serious criminal matters in Osaka, Hyogo (Kobe), and adjacent prefectures. High-profile yakuza trials and corporate fraud cases involving Kansai companies (Kanebo, Duskin scandals) have been heard here. The Osaka High Court sits above it, handling appeals from four western Japan districts.
laws.penalty: N/A — jurisdictional provision, not penal

quiz.q: Which court handles appeals from Osaka District Court's criminal decisions?
quiz.explanation: The Osaka High Court (大阪高等裁判所) handles criminal and civil appeals from Osaka District Court and four other western Japan districts.

laws.title: Universal Health Insurance — Osaka Implementation
laws.subtitle: Osaka's NHI premium non-payment rate among Japan's highest
laws.fullDescription: Osaka City consistently records one of Japan's highest rates of National Health Insurance (NHI) premium non-payment — estimated at 16% of eligible enrollees — reflecting the city's higher poverty rate. The Osaka City Government operates targeted outreach and payment plan programmes. Chronic non-payers may have benefits restricted to emergency-only coverage. This creates a de facto access gap despite universal coverage in principle.
laws.penalty: Premium garnishment from wages or assets; benefits restricted to 6-month vouchers for persistent non-payers
exceptions: Hardship waiver programmes for lowest-income households
laws.sourceLabel: Osaka City — National Health Insurance Division

quiz.q: What distinguishes Osaka City's NHI non-payment rate compared to Japan's national average?
options: Osaka has the lowest non-payment rate
Osaka is at the national average
Osaka has one of Japan's highest non-payment rates (~16%)
Osaka has eliminated non-payment through automation
quiz.explanation: Osaka City's NHI premium non-payment rate of approximately 16% is among Japan's highest — reflecting the city's elevated poverty levels.

laws.title: Video Game and Arcade Machine Copyright
laws.subtitle: Osaka's gaming industry subject to Copyright Act
laws.fullDescription: Osaka is home to major game developers (Capcom, Konami — both headquartered or developed significantly in Osaka/Kobe region). The Copyright Act (著作権法) protects video games as cinematographic works, giving rights holders control over reproduction, public display, and modification. Unauthorized ROM dumping, emulator distribution, and cheating device manufacturing have all been prosecuted in Osaka courts. Game preservation by libraries is a grey area under discussion.
laws.penalty: Unauthorised game reproduction/distribution: up to 10 years imprisonment or ¥10,000,000 fine
exceptions: Fair use for criticism, commentary, and educational purposes
laws.sourceLabel: Agency for Cultural Affairs — Software Copyright

quiz.q: Which major game company is headquartered in Osaka?
quiz.explanation: Capcom (Street Fighter, Resident Evil, Monster Hunter) is headquartered in Osaka — one of Japan's major game publishers based outside Tokyo.

laws.title: Manzai Comedy Performance Licensing
laws.subtitle: Commercial entertainment venues require amusement business licence
laws.fullDescription: Osaka is the birthplace and centre of manzai (漫才) — the two-person stand-up comedy style that dominates Japanese popular culture through agencies like Yoshimoto Kogyo. Live comedy venues, theatres, and performance spaces require Amusement Business licences (風営法) from the Osaka Public Safety Commission. Content regulations exist: performances must not incite discrimination or be obscene. Osaka's Namba Grand Kagetsu theatre is the industry's premier venue.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed commercial performance venue: up to 6 months imprisonment or ¥1,000,000 fine
exceptions: Free public performances in parks with permit; shrine/temple events

quiz.q: What is 'manzai' — the traditional comedy form associated with Osaka?
quiz.explanation: Manzai (漫才) is a traditional Japanese comedy form featuring two performers (boke and tsukkomi) in rapid-fire dialogue — Osaka's most iconic cultural export.

laws.title: Osaka Underground Mall Flood Safety
laws.subtitle: World's largest underground shopping network — strict safety rules
laws.fullDescription: Osaka's underground shopping complex (地下街) — Crysta Nagahori, Whity Umeda, Diamor, etc. — is the world's largest urban underground retail network by area. Under the Fire Service Act and Building Standards Act, these spaces have comprehensive flood emergency protocols, automatic flood gates (止水板), and evacuation procedures given the risk of surface flooding in a Nankai Trough event. Inspection and drill compliance is mandatory.
laws.penalty: Fire/safety code violations in underground malls: closure orders; operators: up to ¥10,000,000 fines
exceptions: Emergency renovation work with approval

quiz.q: What feature of Osaka's underground malls protects against tsunami flooding?
quiz.explanation: Osaka's underground shopping malls install automatic flood gates (止水板) as part of mandatory safety protocols for tsunami scenarios.

laws.title: Kuromon Market Vendor Standards
laws.subtitle: Osaka's kitchen market subject to strict hygiene licensing
laws.fullDescription: Kuromon Ichiba (黒門市場), Osaka's historic fresh produce and seafood market ('Osaka's Kitchen'), operates under strict Food Sanitation Act requirements. Each vendor must hold individual food handling certification. The market has expanded to allow direct retail eating (eat-while-walking) — a shift requiring additional hygiene standards for prepared foods sold for immediate consumption. The Osaka Health Centre conducts regular inspections.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed food preparation/sale: up to ¥500,000 fine and closure; hygiene violations: immediate suspension
exceptions: Non-food vendors exempt from food sanitation requirements
laws.sourceLabel: Osaka City Health Department — Market Inspection

quiz.q: What nickname is given to Kuromon Ichiba market, reflecting its role in Osaka's food culture?
quiz.explanation: Kuromon Ichiba (黒門市場) is known as 'Osaka's Kitchen' — a fresh produce, seafood, and food market central to the city's culinary identity.

laws.title: Osaka Barrier-Free Promotion — Station Lifts
laws.subtitle: All major Osaka Metro stations mandated lift-accessible
laws.fullDescription: Under the Barrier-Free Act and Osaka City's own accessibility ordinance, all Osaka Metro stations must achieve 100% lift accessibility. As of 2024, 97 of 130 Osaka Metro stations have lifts covering all platforms. The 2025 Expo drove accelerated investment in accessibility. Osaka City also operates a guaranteed taxi subsidy for wheelchair users where no accessible public transport route is available.
laws.penalty: New infrastructure projects not meeting barrier-free standards: planning refusal
exceptions: Micro-stations (below 3,000 daily users) have extended compliance timelines

quiz.q: What percentage of Osaka Metro's 130 stations had lift access as of 2024?
quiz.explanation: As of 2024, 97 of Osaka Metro's 130 stations (~75%) had full lift accessibility — with the remainder under construction.

laws.title: Shinkansen Stop at Shin-Osaka
laws.subtitle: High-speed rail regulations at Osaka's main hub
laws.fullDescription: Shin-Osaka Station is Osaka's main Shinkansen terminal, connecting to Tokyo (2h30m), Hiroshima, and Hakata. Under the Shinkansen regulations (新幹線鉄道構造規則), security screening at Shin-Osaka is not mandatory (unlike aviation) but prohibited items include flammable materials, certain chemicals, and large items without reservation. Bicycle carriage requires a bicycle bag and reservation. JR West operates the Sanyo Shinkansen from Shin-Osaka.
laws.penalty: Carrying prohibited items on Shinkansen: ejection from train; bomb threats: up to 3 years imprisonment
exceptions: Folding bicycles in dedicated bags require no reservation

quiz.q: Approximately how long does the Shinkansen take from Tokyo to Shin-Osaka (Nozomi service)?
quiz.explanation: The Nozomi Shinkansen covers Tokyo–Shin-Osaka in approximately 2 hours 30 minutes — one of the world's fastest regular rail services.

laws.title: Osaka Property Tax — Rates and Assessment
laws.subtitle: Fixed asset tax at 1.4% of assessed value
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Local Tax Act (地方税法) sets the standard fixed asset tax rate at 1.4% of the government-assessed value of land and buildings. Osaka City sets its own urban planning tax (都市計画税) of up to 0.3% on top. Tokyo and Osaka have the highest assessed property values in Japan. Osaka's assessed values are recalculated every three years; a small-scale residential land reduction applies (assessed at 1/6 of value for the first 200m²).
laws.penalty: Late payment: 2.6–8.9% surcharge; refusal to pay: attachment of assets
exceptions: Agricultural land in designated zones has reduced assessment rates
laws.sourceLabel: Osaka City — Fixed Asset Tax Division

quiz.q: At what rate is Japan's standard fixed asset tax (property tax) set under the Local Tax Act?
quiz.explanation: Japan's fixed asset tax is set at 1.4% of the government-assessed value — plus an urban planning tax of up to 0.3% in cities like Osaka.

laws.title: Osaka Air Quality — Industrial Zone Monitoring
laws.subtitle: Kishiwada and Sakai industrial zones under emission caps
laws.fullDescription: Osaka Prefecture's southern industrial belt — including Sakai City (steel, chemical), Kishiwada, and the Osaka Bay coastline — is subject to the Air Pollution Control Act (大気汚染防止法) and Osaka's own enhanced emission standards. Sakai City hosts one of Japan's last large integrated steel plants. Osaka Prefecture operates 30 continuous monitoring stations. PM2.5 standards are 35 µg/m³ (24-hour average) — aligned with Japan's national standard.
laws.penalty: Exceeding emission limits: suspension orders + fines up to ¥1,000,000; chronic violators: licence revocation
exceptions: Emergency flaring events with notification

quiz.q: What major industry is concentrated in Osaka's Sakai City on the bay coast?
quiz.explanation: Sakai City hosts one of Japan's last large integrated steel plants plus chemical industries — Osaka's industrial south continues significant heavy manufacturing.

laws.title: Illegal Solicitation — Namba Entertainment
laws.subtitle: Touting and aggressive solicitation prohibited
laws.fullDescription: Osaka's Nuisance Prevention Ordinance (迷惑防止条例) — more recently reinforced by specific Osaka City rules for the Namba entertainment district — prohibits kyaku-hiki (客引き, aggressive customer solicitation) by touts for restaurants, hostess bars, and nightclubs. Police conduct regular enforcement operations particularly on Dotonbori-dori and Sennichimae. Businesses employing illegal touts face licencing consequences.
laws.penalty: Touting in prohibited areas: fines up to ¥100,000 per incident; repeat offenders: up to 6 months imprisonment
exceptions: Approved promotional activities with city permit
laws.sourceLabel: Osaka Prefectural Police — Public Safety Division

quiz.q: What is the Japanese term for the aggressive restaurant/bar touting prohibited in Osaka's entertainment districts?
quiz.explanation: Kyaku-hiki (客引き) — literally 'customer pulling' — refers to touts who aggressively solicit customers into establishments, prohibited in Osaka's entertainment zones.

laws.title: Cannabis Control — Osaka Enforcement
laws.subtitle: National cannabis ban equally enforced in Osaka
laws.fullDescription: The Cannabis Control Act applies equally in Osaka as in Tokyo. Osaka Port has been a noted entry point for cannabis imports, and the Prefectural Police narcotics division conducts active port-area enforcement. Cannabis use among younger Osaka residents has been a growing concern per police statistics — arrests increased 40% between 2018 and 2023, though overall numbers remain low by global standards.
laws.penalty: Possession: up to 5 years; cultivation/import: up to 7 years
exceptions: Industrial hemp under licence
Approved cannabis medicines (from 2024)

quiz.q: By how much did cannabis-related arrests in Osaka increase between 2018 and 2023?
quiz.explanation: Cannabis arrests in Osaka increased approximately 40% between 2018 and 2023 — driven primarily by younger urban users.

laws.title: Osaka International Schools and Licensing
laws.subtitle: International schools require prefectural miscellaneous school approval
laws.fullDescription: International schools in Osaka (including international divisions of Japanese schools and foreign-curriculum schools for expat families) are licenced under the Miscellaneous School (各種学校) category of the School Education Act, as most don't meet criteria for standard category schools. Osaka has approximately 15 international schools serving its significant expat business community (Korean, Chinese, Western). MEXT approves international baccalaureate programmes separately.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed school operation: closure orders + fines; misrepresenting accreditation: fraud charges
exceptions: Short-term supplementary language programmes under certain thresholds

quiz.q: What school licensing category covers most international schools in Japan?
options: Special needs school (特別支援学校)
quiz.explanation: Most international schools in Japan are licenced under the Miscellaneous School (各種学校) category as they don't meet standard curriculum requirements.

laws.title: Osaka Freehold vs Leasehold Land Rules
laws.subtitle: Shakuchiiken land lease system common in Osaka
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Land Lease and Building Lease Act (借地借家法) allows construction on land owned by others via long-term lease (借地権, shakuchiiken). Osaka has a notably high proportion of buildings on leased land compared to Tokyo, reflecting historical land tenure patterns. Fixed-term land leases (定期借地権) set for 50 years were introduced in 1992. Tenants have strong renewal rights under standard leases; eviction requires substantial compensation.
laws.penalty: Landlord illegally refusing lease renewal: civil damages; self-help eviction (changing locks): criminal property damage + civil tort
exceptions: Fixed-term leases (定期借地権) do not auto-renew — landlord can repossess at end of term
laws.sourceLabel: MLIT — Land Lease and Building Lease Act

quiz.q: What is shakuchiiken (借地権) in Japanese property law?
options: A long-term land lease allowing building construction on another's land
quiz.explanation: Shakuchiiken (借地権) is a long-term land lease right that allows the holder to construct and own buildings on land owned by another party.

laws.title: Food Allergy Disclosure — Restaurant Duty
laws.subtitle: Osaka restaurants must disclose allergen information
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Food Labelling Act's allergen disclosure requirements — 7 mandatory allergens including wheat, egg, milk, buckwheat, peanut, shrimp, crab — apply to packaged foods. Osaka's Consumer Affairs Bureau operates voluntary guidance for restaurants to display allergen information. After a 2013 Tokyo school lunch incident (a child died from anaphylaxis), Osaka schools implemented mandatory staff allergen training and parental consent protocols for school meals.
laws.penalty: Restaurant operators: civil liability for allergen-related incidents if no disclosure; criminal negligence if staff grossly failed duty of care
exceptions: Establishments can refer customers to ingredients lists rather than menu labelling

quiz.q: How many allergens are mandatorily disclosed on Japanese food packaging?
quiz.explanation: Japan mandates disclosure of 7 allergens: wheat, buckwheat, egg, milk, peanut, shrimp, and crab — on all packaged food products.

laws.title: Osaka Ishin no Kai Electoral Dominance
laws.subtitle: Regional party controls prefectural and city governments
laws.fullDescription: Osaka Ishin no Kai (Japan Innovation Party — Osaka wing) has governed Osaka Prefecture and City since 2008, making it Japan's most successful regional political movement. Under Public Offices Election Act (公職選挙法) rules, Osaka has twice voted in referendums on the Osaka Metropolis Plan (2015: rejected; 2020: rejected by 0.07%). The party's platform of administrative reform and fiscal consolidation operates within standard Japanese electoral law.
laws.penalty: Election law violations: up to 3 years imprisonment; referendum procedural violations: administrative penalties
laws.sourceLabel: Ministry of Internal Affairs — Election Management

quiz.q: By what margin did Osaka's second referendum on the Osaka Metropolis Plan fail in 2020?
quiz.explanation: The 2020 Osaka Metropolis Plan referendum was rejected by just 0.07% (approximately 17,000 votes out of 2.2 million) — the narrowest margin in Japanese referendum history.

laws.title: Osaka's Fiscal Reconstruction — Debt Reduction Law
laws.subtitle: Prefecture under fiscal reconstruction programme
laws.fullDescription: Osaka Prefecture was placed under a financial reconstruction programme by the Ministry of Internal Affairs in the mid-2000s after years of deficit spending, with debt peaking at ¥7 trillion. Under the Local Finance Law (地方財政法), prefectures in fiscal crisis cannot issue new bonds without ministerial approval and must implement cost-cutting plans. Osaka's reforms under Ishin no Kai governance reduced per-capita spending significantly but also generated controversy over service cuts.
laws.penalty: Non-compliant fiscal reconstruction plans: national government can withhold local allocation tax grants
laws.sourceLabel: Ministry of Internal Affairs — Local Finance

quiz.q: At its peak, approximately how much did Osaka Prefecture's debt reach before its fiscal reconstruction?
quiz.explanation: Osaka Prefecture's debt peaked at approximately ¥7 trillion in the mid-2000s, triggering a national government-supervised fiscal reconstruction programme.

laws.title: Osaka Industrial Safety Standards
laws.subtitle: Industrial Accident Prevention Association enforces workplace safety
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Industrial Safety and Health Act (労働安全衛生法) requires employers in manufacturing, construction, and chemical industries to appoint safety officers, conduct regular inspections, and report serious accidents to the Labour Standards Inspection Office. Osaka's manufacturing and chemical industries (Sumitomo Chemical, Daikin headquarters) must maintain detailed safety management systems. The Osaka Labour Bureau has specialised industrial accident prevention advisers.
laws.penalty: Serious workplace accidents with negligence: up to 6 months imprisonment; failure to report: fines up to ¥500,000
exceptions: Very small workshops (under 10 workers) have simplified requirements

quiz.q: Which major chemical/HVAC company is headquartered in Osaka?
quiz.explanation: Daikin Industries — the world's largest air conditioning manufacturer — is headquartered in Osaka and subject to its industrial safety framework.

laws.title: Osaka Sakura Cherry Blossom Viewing Rules
laws.subtitle: Hanami parties regulated in Osaka Castle Park
laws.fullDescription: Cherry blossom viewing (花見, hanami) at Osaka Castle Park and other designated sites is subject to Osaka City park management rules. Alcohol is permitted but disorderly behaviour is subject to the Nuisance Prevention Ordinance. Blue tarpaulins ('blue sheets') for space reservation from the previous night are officially discouraged; Osaka Castle Park management may remove tarpaulins laid more than 24 hours ahead. Open fires are prohibited in all parks.
laws.penalty: Prohibited fires in parks: fines under Fire Service Act; disorderly drunk conduct: up to ¥50,000 under Nuisance Ordinance
exceptions: Licensed food/drink vendors in designated park zones

quiz.q: What is the traditional Japanese practice of gathering under cherry trees called?
quiz.explanation: Hanami (花見, 'flower viewing') is the traditional practice of gathering under cherry blossom trees to eat, drink, and celebrate spring.

laws.title: Osaka's Arson History and Prevention
laws.subtitle: Historic fire risk in Osaka's wooden district housing
laws.fullDescription: Osaka's dense traditional machiya (町家) wooden townhouse districts in areas like Namba, Tsuruhashi, and Juso remain significant fire risks. The Fire Service Act requires these older wooden buildings to install sprinkler systems above 275m² total floor area. Osaka City has an intensive building survey programme targeting unoccupied wooden structures. Fire safety inspections of entertainment venues (izakaya, karaoke) are mandated annually.
laws.penalty: Arson: up to life imprisonment (inhabited buildings); fire safety violations: closure orders + fines up to ¥3,000,000
exceptions: Designated cultural properties may receive exemptions if historic fabric would be damaged by sprinkler installation — alternative fire protection required

quiz.q: What traditional Japanese wooden townhouse building type is common in Osaka's older districts?
quiz.explanation: Machiya (町家) are traditional wooden merchant townhouses — common in Osaka's older commercial districts and a significant fire risk requiring special safety measures.

laws.title: Yoshimoto Kogyo Talent Agency Compliance
laws.subtitle: Japan's largest talent agency subject to fair business rules
laws.fullDescription: Yoshimoto Kogyo (吉本興業), headquartered in Osaka and managing over 6,000 comedians and entertainers, operates under the Employment Security Act (職業安定法) as a talent agency. 2019 scandals involving talent receiving undisclosed yakuza-connected event payments led to a parliamentary inquiry and industry-wide guidance on contract transparency and exclusivity clauses. The Fair Trade Commission reviewed Yoshimoto's exclusive contract practices.
laws.penalty: Talent agencies engaging in unfair exclusive practices: FTC cease-and-desist; illegal undisclosed fee arrangements: up to ¥1,000,000 fine

quiz.q: Approximately how many comedians and entertainers does Osaka's Yoshimoto Kogyo manage?
quiz.explanation: Yoshimoto Kogyo manages over 6,000 entertainers — making it Japan's largest and most powerful talent agency, headquartered in Osaka.

laws.title: Vaccination Requirements — School Entry
laws.subtitle: Recommended vaccinations technically voluntary but socially mandated
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Immunisation Act (予防接種法) designates scheduled vaccinations (定期接種) for children including BCG, DPT, IPV, MMR (though Japan uses MR), varicella, Hib, and pneumococcal. These are technically voluntary but Osaka City schools and day-care centres track vaccination records and may contact parents about unvaccinated children. Japan had a major measles resurgence in 2018–2019 linked to vaccination gaps, prompting stricter monitoring.
laws.penalty: Vaccines are not legally mandatory; no criminal penalty; social/administrative pressure via school contact
exceptions: Medical exemptions with doctor's certificate
laws.sourceLabel: Osaka City Health and Welfare Bureau — Immunisation

quiz.q: What disease caused a major Osaka/Japan-wide resurgence in 2018–2019 due to vaccination gaps?
quiz.explanation: Japan experienced a significant measles (麻疹) resurgence in 2018–2019 linked to vaccination gaps — WHO issued travel warnings for Japan.

laws.title: Osaka Kansai Airport Customs Rules
laws.subtitle: Strict duty-free allowances and prohibited items
laws.fullDescription: Kansai International Airport (KIX), serving Osaka and the wider Kansai region, operates under Japan Customs Act (関税法) rules: duty-free allowances include 200 cigarettes, 3 bottles of alcohol (760ml each), and personal items up to ¥200,000 in value. Agricultural products (fresh meat, vegetables, fruits) from many countries are prohibited under Plant Protection Act and Law Concerning Special Measures against Infectious Diseases. Random baggage inspection rates at KIX are among Japan's highest.
laws.penalty: Duty evasion: 3× the evaded duty + criminal penalties up to 10 years; prohibited agricultural import: confiscation + fines up to ¥500,000
exceptions: Commercial imports follow separate tariff schedule and licencing

quiz.q: What is the duty-free personal goods allowance for travellers entering Japan?
options: No limit — all personal use items are free
quiz.explanation: Travellers to Japan may bring in personal goods up to ¥200,000 in value duty-free (in addition to alcohol and tobacco allowances).

laws.title: Freedom of Assembly — Osaka Protest Rules
laws.subtitle: Demonstrations require advance police notification
laws.fullDescription: Under Japan's Road Traffic Act and prefectural public safety ordinances, demonstrations and marches using public roads require advance notification to and approval from the Osaka Prefectural Public Safety Commission (公安委員会). Notification must be submitted 72 hours in advance. Counter-demonstrations and impromptu gatherings have led to confrontations in Osaka, particularly involving Korean minority communities and right-wing groups. Police may impose route modifications.
laws.penalty: Unnotified demonstrations: organisers fined up to ¥300,000; violent protests: assault/obstruction charges
exceptions: Private property gatherings require no public safety approval
laws.sourceLabel: Osaka Prefectural Police — Public Safety Commission

quiz.q: How far in advance must demonstration organisers notify Osaka's Public Safety Commission?
quiz.explanation: Osaka's road-use demonstration notification must be submitted 72 hours before the event to the Prefectural Public Safety Commission.

laws.title: Osaka Green Innovation Strategy 2030
laws.subtitle: Osaka targeting 50% renewable energy by 2030
laws.fullDescription: Osaka Prefecture's Green Innovation Strategy (グリーンイノベーション戦略, 2021) targets 50% renewable energy in the prefecture's own facilities by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2050. Companies operating in Osaka's designated green innovation zones receive tax incentives under prefectural ordinance. Osaka Gas (now Daigas) is a major energy provider transitioning to hydrogen and biogas. The hydrogen technology cluster around Osaka is Japan's most developed.
laws.penalty: N/A — incentive-based strategy; mandatory components for large emitters: annual reporting with financial penalties for non-reporting

quiz.q: What energy transition technology cluster around Osaka is considered Japan's most advanced?
quiz.explanation: Osaka's industrial base, including Daigas and Kawasaki Heavy Industries, makes the Osaka/Kobe corridor Japan's leading hydrogen technology development cluster.

laws.title: Historical Sex Work Regulation — Osaka
laws.subtitle: Prostitution prohibited; related businesses licenced
laws.fullDescription: The Prostitution Prevention Law (売春防止法, 1956) prohibits selling or buying sex in Japan. However, the 'sexual services' industry (風俗産業) operates extensively through businesses technically selling 'companionship' rather than sex. In Osaka, designated entertainment zones (Tobita Shinchi being Japan's most famous de facto red-light district) operate in a complex legal grey zone tolerated by local police. Tobita Shinchi is officially a restaurant cluster.
laws.penalty: Prostitution: up to 1 year imprisonment or ¥30,000 fine (historically rarely enforced against individuals); pimping/trafficking: up to 10 years
exceptions: Licensed 'fuzoku' businesses selling legal sexual services short of intercourse (e.g. massage, soaplands)

quiz.q: What is Tobita Shinchi — officially described as a 'restaurant district' in Osaka?
options: Japan's most famous de facto red-light district operating in a legal grey zone
A film studio and entertainment complex
quiz.explanation: Tobita Shinchi (飛田新地) is Japan's most famous de facto red-light district, officially operating as a 'restaurant' district in a complex legal grey zone tolerated by Osaka authorities.

laws.title: Osaka Nighttime Economy — Club Licensing
laws.subtitle: 2015 reform allowed dancing after midnight
laws.fullDescription: The 2015 amendment to Japan's Businesses Affecting Public Morals Act (風営法) removed the restriction prohibiting dancing in nightclubs after midnight — a rule dating from 1948. This was a significant win for Osaka's nightlife scene, which had been suppressed by police enforcement (Club Noon raid 2010, Club Metro Kyoto 2012). Osaka's American Village (アメ村) and south Shinsaibashi club district benefited most. Clubs still require licences and must prevent crime and drug use.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed club operation: up to 2 years imprisonment; drug/crime-related violations: licence revocation
exceptions: Restaurants with incidental music/entertainment have different classification
laws.sourceLabel: NPA — Businesses Affecting Public Morals Act 2015

quiz.q: From what year did Japan's law prohibiting dancing in clubs after midnight originate?
quiz.explanation: Japan's ban on post-midnight dancing originated from a 1948 law — still enforced until the 2015 amendment finally removed the restriction.

laws.title: MUFG and Osaka Banking History
laws.subtitle: Major banks subject to FSA oversight from Osaka origins
laws.fullDescription: Osaka was historically Japan's financial capital (Edo-era commodity trading) before Tokyo assumed dominance. Major financial groups with Osaka roots — Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG), Osaka Gas Finance — remain subject to FSA regulation. The Bank of Japan's Osaka branch is the institution's most important regional office. Under the Banking Act (銀行法), all banks must hold capital adequacy ratios meeting Basel III standards (minimum 8% for internationally active banks).
laws.penalty: Capital ratio violations: mandatory remediation orders → bank closure proceedings
exceptions: Cooperative credit unions (信用組合) operate under separate cooperative banking law with lower minimums

quiz.q: What is the minimum Basel III capital adequacy ratio for internationally active Japanese banks?
quiz.explanation: Basel III requires internationally active banks to maintain a minimum 8% total capital ratio — enforced by Japan's FSA under the Banking Act.

laws.title: Osaka Monorail and Airport Link Rules
laws.subtitle: Osaka Monorail connects to Itami Airport and Expo site
laws.fullDescription: The Osaka Monorail (大阪モノレール) — the world's longest monorail by route length at 28.4km — connects Itami Airport, Osaka University, and will extend to Nakamozu by 2029. Under the Railway Business Act (鉄道事業法), the monorail is regulated as a standard railway. Its extension to the Expo 2025 site and future Yumeshima IR area is a key infrastructure project. Ticket inspection and fare payment are mandatory — evasion prosecuted as with other railways.
laws.penalty: Fare evasion: back-fare + surcharge; refusal: civil/criminal proceedings

quiz.q: What distinction does the Osaka Monorail hold by route length?
quiz.explanation: At 28.4km, the Osaka Monorail holds the Guinness World Record as the world's longest monorail line by total route length.

laws.title: Osaka Metropolitan Area Urban Renewal
laws.subtitle: Urban Renewal Act enables rapid redevelopment
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Act on Special Measures for Urban Regeneration (都市再生特別措置法, 2002) creates special urban regeneration zones where normal planning restrictions are relaxed to attract private investment. Osaka has designated several zones including Umeda/Grand Front Osaka, Nakanoshima, and Nanko Port Town. Within these zones, developers can exceed normal floor area ratios in exchange for public space contributions. The Osaka Metropolis Plan's rejection hasn't impacted these national-law-based zones.
laws.penalty: Development outside approved zone parameters: planning refusal → enforcement order
exceptions: Emergency infrastructure (utilities, flood works) exempt from standard planning timeline
laws.sourceLabel: MLIT — Urban Regeneration Special Measures Act

quiz.q: What major Osaka development created around Osaka Station exemplifies the Urban Regeneration Act?
quiz.explanation: Grand Front Osaka (グランフロント大阪) in Umeda was developed under Urban Regeneration Zone designation, allowing greater height and density than normal planning rules permit.

laws.title: Maternity and Childcare Benefits — Osaka
laws.subtitle: Osaka City provides supplementary childcare support
laws.fullDescription: Beyond national maternity benefits (67% of salary for 6 weeks before + 8 weeks after birth; 50% for parental leave), Osaka City provides supplementary childcare subsidies and operates 'Osaka City nursery waitlist reduction' measures. As of 2024, Osaka City has eliminated nursery school waitlists — a major policy success following Tokyo's high-profile 'I can't get into nursery!' (保育園落ちた日本死ね) blog post that sparked national outrage in 2016.
laws.penalty: Employers failing to pay national maternity benefits: administrative guidance; dismissing pregnant employees: civil tort + compensation
exceptions: Fixed-term workers must meet qualifying period requirements

quiz.q: What achievement has Osaka City accomplished regarding nursery school waitlists?
quiz.explanation: Osaka City eliminated nursery school waitlists by 2024 — a notable policy success in a country where childcare shortages sparked national outrage in 2016.

laws.title: Credit Card Fraud — Osaka Tech Enforcement
laws.subtitle: Card skimming and cyber fraud prosecuted under Fraud Act
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Penal Code fraud provisions and the Act on Prohibition of Unauthorised Computer Access (不正アクセス禁止法) cover credit card fraud, skimming device installation, and online payment fraud. Osaka, with Japan's second-highest number of credit card transactions, sees significant fraud enforcement. The Osaka Prefectural Police Cybercrime Division investigates international card fraud rings and domestic skimming operations at ATMs and restaurants.
laws.penalty: Credit card fraud: up to 10 years imprisonment (fraud); skimming device use: up to 10 years; unauthorised computer access: up to 3 years

quiz.q: What Japanese law specifically prohibits unauthorised computer access — used to prosecute online fraud?
options: Act on Prohibition of Unauthorised Computer Access (不正アクセス禁止法)
quiz.explanation: Japan's Act on Prohibition of Unauthorised Computer Access (不正アクセス禁止法) is the main law used to prosecute hacking, credential theft, and online fraud.

laws.title: Osaka Expo 2025 Security Zone
laws.subtitle: Special security regulations around Expo site
laws.fullDescription: Osaka's Expo 2025 (April 13–October 13, 2025, Yumeshima island) operates under special security regulations under the Act on Security Measures for Facilities Hosting International Events. A security perimeter surrounds the 155-hectare site. Designated prohibited items include standard dangerous goods. Police and Japan Self-Defense Force personnel provide integrated security. Foreign government pavilions have diplomatic protection under the Vienna Convention.
laws.penalty: Security zone violations: removal and fine; prohibited item carrying: confiscation and fines
exceptions: Diplomatic staff with accreditation
Emergency services
laws.sourceLabel: Japan Association for the 2025 World Exposition — Security

quiz.q: Over what time period does Osaka Expo 2025 run?
quiz.explanation: Osaka Expo 2025 runs for 6 months, from April 13 to October 13, 2025 — following the standard World Expo duration.

laws.title: Osaka's 'Midori no Kaze' Greening Plan
laws.subtitle: Street tree planting and greenery corridor targets
laws.fullDescription: Osaka City's Midori no Kaze (緑の風) — Green Wind — urban greenery plan targets increasing street tree canopy along major corridors including Midosuji Boulevard (御堂筋), Osaka's grand Champs-Élysées equivalent, lined with iconic ginkgo trees. The plan requires new roadside developments to plant trees at specified intervals. Osaka Castle moat's cherry trees are managed under heritage landscape rules. The plan aims for 20% green coverage.
laws.penalty: Development projects removing street trees without replacement: planning conditions enforced; fines for unauthorised tree removal up to ¥500,000
exceptions: Emergency utility works with replanting obligation

quiz.q: What iconic tree lines Osaka's grand Midosuji Boulevard — often compared to the Champs-Élysées?
quiz.explanation: Midosuji Boulevard is famous for its rows of ginkgo trees — creating a stunning golden canopy in autumn — protected under Osaka's greenery plans.

laws.title: E-Commerce Act — Online Retail Compliance
laws.subtitle: Osaka's tech firms must comply with online sales law
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Act on Specified Commercial Transactions (特定商取引法) governs online retail, requiring e-commerce operators to display business name, address, phone number, pricing, and return policies clearly. Osaka-based online retailers (including Rakuten — founded in Kobe, operating from Tokyo) are monitored by the Consumer Affairs Agency. 'Surprise subscription' (サブスク詐欺) schemes, where consumers unknowingly sign up for recurring charges, have been the subject of major enforcement actions.
laws.penalty: Non-compliant online stores: administrative guidance → fines up to ¥3,000,000; fraudulent subscription schemes: criminal fraud charges up to 10 years
exceptions: B2B online transactions follow separate rules

quiz.q: What deceptive practice (サブスク詐欺) has Japanese online retail regulators targeted in recent years?
options: Surprise subscription schemes — unknowing recurring charges
quiz.explanation: Sabusku-sagi (サブスク詐欺) — surprise subscription fraud — where consumers unknowingly enrol in recurring charges, has been a major Consumer Affairs Agency enforcement target.

laws.title: Osaka Domestic Violence Prevention
laws.subtitle: DV Act provides protection orders for victims
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Act on Prevention of Spousal Violence and Protection of Victims (DV防止法, 2001, amended 2023) allows courts to issue protection orders (保護命令) prohibiting abusers from approaching victims within 100m and from contacting them. Osaka Prefectural Government operates Osaka Spousal Violence Counseling and Support Centre (大阪府配偶者暴力相談支援センター). 2023 amendments expanded protection to dating partners and extended order duration to one year.
laws.penalty: Violation of protection order: up to 1 year imprisonment or ¥1,000,000 fine
exceptions: Mediation and counselling pathways available as alternatives in some cases
laws.sourceLabel: Osaka Prefecture DV Prevention — Spousal Violence Act

quiz.q: What did Japan's 2023 amendments to the Domestic Violence Act expand protection orders to cover?
quiz.explanation: The 2023 DV Act amendments expanded protection orders to cover dating partners — not only married or formerly married couples.

laws.title: Pharmaceutical Manufacturing — Osaka as Japan's Drug Capital
laws.subtitle: Osaka hosts Japan's largest pharmaceutical cluster
laws.fullDescription: Osaka Prefecture hosts the highest concentration of pharmaceutical manufacturers in Japan — including Takeda, Dainippon Sumitomo, Rohto, and Shionogi. The Pharmaceutical and Medical Device Act (薬機法, 2014) regulates manufacturing licences, quality standards (GMP), clinical trials, and drug advertising. The Osaka PMDA (Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency) regional office is a key regulatory contact. Drug advertising in Japan is subject to stricter rules than in the US — DTC advertising is banned.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed drug manufacturing: up to 10 years imprisonment; false advertising: up to 2 years + fines
exceptions: Hospital pharmacy compounding within specific guidelines

quiz.q: Which major global pharmaceutical company is headquartered in Osaka?
quiz.explanation: Takeda Pharmaceutical — Japan's largest and one of the world's top-10 pharma companies — is headquartered in Osaka, though its global HQ is now in Tokyo.

laws.title: Osaka's Small Business Finance Corporation
laws.subtitle: SME loans regulated under Small and Medium Enterprises Basic Act
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Small and Medium Enterprises Basic Act (中小企業基本法) and the Japan Finance Corporation (日本政策金融公庫) provide preferential financing to SMEs. Osaka's dense concentration of small manufacturing businesses (monozukuri — 'making things') benefits from Osaka Prefecture's SME support programmes. The Osaka Business and Investment Centre assists foreign companies establishing Kansai operations. SME loan guarantees are provided by the Osaka Credit Guarantee Association.
laws.penalty: Misuse of government SME finance: loan recall + criminal fraud charges; false financial statements for loan applications: up to 5 years
exceptions: Startups in Osaka's designated 'startup ecosystem' zones have additional support access

quiz.q: What Japanese manufacturing philosophy — 'the art of making things' — characterises Osaka's small business culture?
quiz.explanation: Monozukuri (ものづくり, 'making things') describes Japan's manufacturing philosophy emphasising craftsmanship and quality — especially prevalent in Osaka's dense SME manufacturing sector.

laws.title: Firearms — Osaka Yakuza Gun Seizures
laws.subtitle: Osaka records Japan's highest yakuza-related firearms seizures
laws.fullDescription: Despite Japan's near-total civilian gun ban, the Osaka Prefectural Police Organised Crime Division reports the highest number of yakuza-related firearms seizures in Japan — reflecting the Yamaguchi-gumi and Kudo-kai activity in the Kansai region. Guns typically enter via smuggling from the Philippines and Southeast Asia through Osaka and Kobe ports. Operation Hana-yuki (花雪) and similar targeted operations have reduced seizure numbers since 2018.
laws.penalty: Illegal firearm possession: up to 15 years imprisonment; discharging: additional up to 3 years
laws.sourceLabel: Osaka Prefectural Police — Organised Crime Division

quiz.q: Where do most illegal firearms in Japan originate according to police?
quiz.explanation: Most illegal firearms in Japan are smuggled from the Philippines and Southeast Asia — entering primarily through Osaka and Kobe ports.

laws.title: Osaka Aquarium (Kaiyukan) Animal Welfare Rules
laws.subtitle: Aquarium and zoo animal welfare under Environment Ministry
laws.fullDescription: Osaka's Kaiyukan aquarium — one of the world's largest, featuring a 5.4 million litre Pacific Ocean tank housing whale sharks — operates under the Animal Welfare and Management Act (動物の愛護及び管理に関する法律). Commercial aquariums must maintain species-appropriate conditions, employ certified veterinary staff, and comply with CITES requirements for protected species. The Environment Ministry and Osaka City jointly inspect facilities.
laws.penalty: Animal welfare violations: fines up to ¥500,000; CITES violations: up to 5 years imprisonment

quiz.q: What is the volume of Osaka Kaiyukan's main Pacific Ocean tank — one of the world's largest aquarium tanks?
quiz.explanation: Kaiyukan's Pacific Ocean tank holds 5.4 million litres — one of the world's largest aquarium tanks, housing whale sharks and manta rays.

laws.title: Gacha Loot Box Regulation — Osaka Game Industry
laws.subtitle: Kompu gacha prohibited; random item mechanics regulated
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Consumer Affairs Agency ruled in 2012 that 'complete gacha' (コンプガチャ), a mechanic requiring purchase of random items to complete a set, violates the Act against Unjustifiable Premiums and Misleading Representations as an illegal lottery. Major Osaka-based mobile game developers (including Gungho Online Entertainment, maker of Puzzle & Dragons) had to restructure games. Standard random item gacha (without forced completion mechanics) remains legal but subject to disclosure rules on odds.
laws.penalty: Kompu gacha or non-disclosed odds: cease-and-desist; fines up to 3% of related sales
exceptions: Standard random item gacha with disclosed probabilities is legal

quiz.q: What did Japan's Consumer Affairs Agency rule about 'complete gacha' (コンプガチャ) in 2012?
options: It violates premium representation law as an illegal lottery
quiz.explanation: Japan's CAA ruled in 2012 that complete gacha (requiring set completion through random purchases) violates the Premiums Act — forcing major game developers to redesign mechanics.

laws.title: Child Custody — Single Parent Default
laws.subtitle: Japan's sole custody system challenged by international courts
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Civil Code (民法) historically prescribed sole custody to one parent after divorce, with the other parent having no legal right of contact unless agreed. This caused international incidents when Japanese nationals took children to Japan in international custody disputes. A 2024 Civil Code amendment introduced optional joint custody from 2026 — a historic shift. Osaka Family Court handles significant numbers of international custody cases given the Zainichi and international business community.
laws.penalty: Parental abduction (removing child from Japan without court order): criminal charges under Child Abduction Prohibition Act; international cases: HCCH Abduction Convention (Japan acceded 2014) applies
exceptions: Domestic violence cases may maintain sole custody as default

quiz.q: What major change to Japan's child custody law was enacted in 2024?
options: Mandatory joint custody for all cases
Introduction of optional joint custody from 2026
Creation of a family court arbitration system
quiz.explanation: Japan's 2024 Civil Code amendment introduced optional joint custody from 2026 — a historic departure from the sole-custody default that had caused international disputes.

laws.title: Foreign Worker Integration — Specified Skilled Worker
laws.subtitle: Osaka's manufacturing sector uses new visa categories
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Specified Skilled Worker (特定技能) visa, introduced in 2019, allows foreign workers in 14 designated industries (including food manufacturing, construction, hospitality) to work in Japan without requiring an employer sponsor for visa status. Osaka's food processing and construction sectors are significant employers of Specified Skilled Workers — predominantly from Vietnam, Indonesia, and the Philippines. Osaka Prefectural Government operates multilingual support centres.
laws.penalty: Employers underpaying or mistreating Specified Skilled Workers: labour law penalties + possibility of losing ability to sponsor workers
exceptions: Tier 2 (特定技能2号) workers in certain industries can bring family and have a path to permanent residence
laws.sourceLabel: Immigration Services Agency — Specified Skilled Worker

quiz.q: In which year did Japan introduce the Specified Skilled Worker (特定技能) visa category?
quiz.explanation: Japan introduced the Specified Skilled Worker visa in April 2019 to address acute labour shortages in 14 designated industries.

laws.title: Osaka Smart City Data Governance
laws.subtitle: Osaka's smart city initiative subject to PPC oversight
laws.fullDescription: Osaka City's Smart City Strategy (スマートシティ戦略) uses data from sensors, cameras, and public service systems to manage traffic, waste, and emergency response. Under APPI and Smart City guidelines from the Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC), personal data collected in smart city contexts requires purpose limitation, anonymisation standards, and public disclosure of data use policies. Osaka was designated one of Japan's 10 'super city' zones in 2023.
laws.penalty: APPI violations in smart city data use: up to ¥100,000,000 corporate fine; individual breach notification failures: criminal penalty
exceptions: Anonymised and aggregated statistical data not subject to individual consent requirements

quiz.q: What designation did Osaka receive in 2023 for its advanced urban digital infrastructure?
quiz.explanation: Osaka was designated one of Japan's 10 'Super City' (スーパーシティ) zones in 2023, enabling data-sharing and regulatory innovation for smart urban services.

laws.title: Osaka Castle Site Ownership
laws.subtitle: Castle grounds are national government property managed by city
laws.fullDescription: Osaka Castle's grounds are national government property (国有財産) administered by Osaka City under a management agreement with the Ministry of Finance. The castle tower (天守閣) itself is privately owned by Osaka City and operated as a museum. Any major infrastructure development within the castle park requires national approval. The castle survived WWII bombing but its current tower is a 1931 reinforced concrete reconstruction — not an original wooden structure.
laws.penalty: Damage to national property at castle grounds: up to ¥3,000,000 fine or 5 years imprisonment
exceptions: Permitted heritage-consistent restoration works

quiz.q: When was the current Osaka Castle tower built — and from what material?
quiz.explanation: Osaka Castle's current tower is a 1931 reinforced concrete reconstruction — not an original wooden castle. The original was destroyed in the 1615 Siege of Osaka.

laws.title: Cybercrime — Osaka's International Fraud Rings
laws.subtitle: Osaka Cyber Division targets international fraud operations
laws.fullDescription: The Osaka Prefectural Police Cybercrime Division (サイバー犯罪対策課) investigates computer intrusions, online fraud, cryptocurrency theft, and international business email compromise (BEC) schemes. Osaka has been a base for international crypto fraud operations and call centre scam rings targeting Japanese elderly ('ore ore sagi' — voice fraud). The Act on Prohibition of Unauthorised Computer Access (不正アクセス禁止法) is the primary prosecution tool.
laws.penalty: Unauthorised computer access: up to 3 years; computer fraud: up to 10 years; ore ore sagi (voice fraud): up to 10 years
laws.sourceLabel: Osaka Prefectural Police — Cyber Crime Division

quiz.q: What is 'ore ore sagi' (オレオレ詐欺) — a type of fraud heavily prosecuted in Osaka?
options: Voice/phone fraud where callers impersonate relatives ('It's me, it's me') to steal from elderly
quiz.explanation: Ore ore sagi (オレオレ詐欺, 'it's me, it's me fraud') is a phone scam where criminals impersonate relatives in distress to steal money from elderly victims — a major issue in Japan.

laws.title: EV Charging Infrastructure Mandate
laws.subtitle: New car parks in Osaka must include EV charging
laws.fullDescription: Osaka Prefecture's 2023 ordinance requires new car parks over 50 spaces and new buildings with parking facilities to install EV charging infrastructure for at least 20% of spaces (quick chargers or standard chargers). This exceeds the national Revitalisation Plan standard of 15%. Panasonic, headquartered in Osaka suburb Kadoma, produces EV battery components. Osaka City offers subsidies for residential EV charger installation.
laws.penalty: Non-compliant new construction: planning approval condition not met; retrospective enforcement unlikely except for large commercial facilities
exceptions: Buildings with fewer than 10 car parking spaces

quiz.q: What percentage of new parking spaces in Osaka must include EV charging under the 2023 ordinance?
quiz.explanation: Osaka's 2023 ordinance requires 20% of new parking spaces to have EV charging — exceeding the national 15% standard.

laws.title: Osaka Night Economy Promotion
laws.subtitle: Osaka piloting extended business hours in designated zones
laws.fullDescription: Under a 2023 special zone designation by the national government, Osaka is piloting extended operating hours for bars, restaurants, and entertainment venues in designated night economy promotion zones (夜間経済特区) in Shinsaibashi and Namba. The pilot allows 24-hour operation with enhanced noise management requirements. This aligns with the national government's strategy to boost inbound tourist spending and is linked to Expo 2025 preparation. Results will inform potential national regulatory reform.
laws.penalty: Venues in extended-hours zones violating noise or conduct conditions: zone status revoked; standard Nuisance Ordinance applies
exceptions: The extended hours apply only to businesses registered in the designated zone
laws.sourceLabel: Osaka City — Night Economy Promotion Zone

quiz.q: What national designation enabled Osaka to pilot extended bar/restaurant hours in 2023?
options: Night Economy Promotion Zone (夜間経済特区)
quiz.explanation: Osaka's Night Economy Promotion Zone (夜間経済特区) designation in 2023 enabled pilot 24-hour business operations in Shinsaibashi and Namba, linked to Expo 2025 preparations.
